headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide to a few popular IP‑lookup APIs that return **company‑level data** (organization name, domain, contact details, etc.) when you supply an IP address. All of them expose a simple HTTP GET endpoint that you can hit from any language (Python, JavaScript, curl, Postman, etc.). | Service | Key Features | Free Tier | Typical Endpoint | Example | |---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|---------| | **ipinfo.io** | • Organization name, ASN, domain
• Contact email & phone (if available)
• Geo‑location, carrier, etc. | 50 k requests/month (no key needed for basic data) | `https://ipinfo.io//json` | `https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json` | | **ipstack.com** | • Company name, domain, contact email
• Geo‑location, currency, timezone
• Rich “business” data for paid plans | 10 k requests/month (free key) | `https://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=YOUR_KEY` | `https://api.ipstack.com/8.8.8.8?access_key=12345` | | **ipapi.co** | • Organization, domain, contact email
• Geo‑location, carrier, ASN
• Rate‑limited free tier | 30 k requests/month (free key) | `https://ipapi.co//json/` | `https://ipapi.co/8.8.8.8/json/` | | **ipgeolocation.io** | • Company name, domain, contact email
• Geo‑location, ISP, ASN
• Additional security & threat intel | 1 k requests/day (free key) | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=` | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=12345&ip=8.8.8.8` | | **ipwhois.io** | • Organization, domain, contact email
• Geo‑location, ASN, carrier | 10 k requests/month (free key) | `https://ipwhois.app/json/` | `https://ipwhois.app/json/8.8.8.8` | --- ## How to Use One of These APIs (Python Example) Below is a reusable helper that works with any of the services above. Just swap out the `BASE_URL` and `PARAMS` for the service you choose. ```python import requests def lookup_ip(ip_address: str, service: str = "ipinfo") -> dict: """ Query an IP‑lookup service and return company/contact data. Parameters ---------- ip_address : str The IPv4 or IPv6 address to look up. service : str One of: "ipinfo", "ipstack", "ipapi", "ipgeolocation", "ipwhois". Returns ------- dict Parsed JSON response (or empty dict on error). """ # --- Service configuration ------------------------------------------------- if service == "ipinfo": base_url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip_address}/json" params = {} # no key needed for basic data elif service == "ipstack": base_url = f"https://api.ipstack.com/{ip_address}" params = {"access_key": "YOUR_IPSTACK_KEY"} elif service == "ipapi": base_url = f"https://ipapi.co/{ip_address}/json/" params = {"key": "YOUR_IPAPI_KEY"} elif service == "ipgeolocation": base_url = "https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo" params = {"apiKey": "YOUR_IPGEO_KEY", "ip": ip_address} elif service == "ipwhois": base_url = f"https://ipwhois.app/json/{ip_address}" params = {} else: raise ValueError("Unsupported service") # --- Make the request ------------------------------------------------------ try: resp = requests.get(base_url, params=params, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() data = resp.json() except Exception as e: print(f"Error querying {service}: {e}") data = {} # --- Normalise the response (optional) ------------------------------------ # Many services return slightly different keys; this snippet pulls out # the most common ones so you can use a single interface. company = data.get("org") or data.get("organization") or data.get("company") domain = data.get("domain") or data.get("hostname") contact_email = data.get("email") or data.get("contact_email") contact_phone = data.get("phone") or data.get("contact_phone") return { "ip": ip_address, "company": company, "domain": domain, "contact_email": contact_email, "contact_phone": contact_phone, "raw": data, # keep the full response for debugging } # Example usage if __name__ == "__main__": ip = "8.8.8.8" result = lookup_ip(ip, service="ipinfo") print(result) ``` ### What You’ll Get | Field | Typical Value | Notes | |-------|---------------|-------| | `company` | `"Google LLC"` | May be `None` if the IP isn’t tied to a registered org. | | `domain` | `"google.com"` | Some services return the domain of the organization. | | `contact_email` | `"support@google.com"` | Only available on paid plans or for certain IP ranges. | | `contact_phone` | `"+1-650-253-0000"` | Same as above. | | `raw` | Full JSON | Useful for debugging or accessing fields not normalised. | --- ## Choosing the Right Service | Criteria | ipinfo.io | ipstack.com | ipapi.co | ipgeolocation.io | ipwhois.io | |----------|-----------|-------------|----------|------------------|------------| | **Free tier** | 50 k/month | 10 k/month | 30 k/month | 1 k/day | 10 k/month | | **Contact data** | Yes (paid) | Yes (paid) | Yes (paid) | Yes (paid) | Yes (paid) | | **Rate limit** | 1 k/min | 1 k/min | 1 k/min | 1 k/min | 1 k/min | | **Ease of use** | Very simple | Simple | Simple | Simple | Simple | | **Pricing (paid)** | $50/mo for 1 M reqs | $99/mo for 1 M reqs | $49/mo for 1 M reqs | $49/mo for 1 M reqs | $49/mo for 1 M reqs | | **Best for** | Quick prototyping | Enterprise‑grade data | Balanced | Security + business data | Lightweight | **Tip:** If you only need the *company name* and *domain*, the free tiers of all services are usually sufficient. For *contact email/phone*, you’ll need a paid plan or a dedicated business‑lookup service (e.g., Clearbit, FullContact, or Hunter.io). --- ## Privacy & Legal Considerations 1. **GDPR / CCPA** – IP addresses are considered personal data in many jurisdictions. *If you store or process the data, ensure you have a lawful basis (e.g., legitimate interest, consent).* 2. **Data Accuracy** – IP‑to‑company mapping is not always 100 % accurate. *Always validate critical data before using it in production.* 3. **Rate Limits** – Exceeding the free tier will trigger throttling or bans. *Implement exponential back‑off or caching.* 4. **Terms of Service** – Most APIs forbid bulk scraping or redistribution of raw data. *Read the TOS carefully before integrating.* --- ## Next Steps 1. **Pick a provider** based on your budget and required fields. 2. **Sign up** for an API key (if needed). 3. **Integrate** the helper function into your codebase. 4. **Cache** results (e.g., Redis, in‑memory dict) to stay within rate limits. 5. **Add error handling** for cases where the provider returns `null` or `404`. Happy coding! If you need help wiring this into a specific framework (FastAPI, Flask, Node.js, etc.) or setting up caching, just let me know.
